The Laredo City Council voted Nov. 3 to authorize the city manager to spend up to $400,000 to launch a feral hog control program and hire a contractor, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

The program will focus on parks, public land and water sources, with the city also buying equipment. It could begin within 30 to 60 days, District 6 Council Member Tyler King said — late November or early December, and before Christmas if the schedule holds.

About 200 hogs are in the Laredo area, concentrated in north Laredo, the report says, and residents have complained about damage to water and sewer infrastructure. The city plans to use drones and infrared technology to identify hog activity and prepare bait sites, and it will first survey the hog population, locations and health risks, Health Services Director Dr. Hector F. Gonzalez said.

On cost, Environmental Services Director Robert A. Neeb put equipment at an estimated $175,000, while King said the first year would run about $400,000 — roughly $200,000 for equipment and $200,000 for services.

Statewide, about 2.6 million feral hogs in Texas cause about $400 million in damage each year, according to the report.

Source: Laredo Morning Times, Nov. 5, 2026 (César Rodriguez).
